counterfactual_missing_items: No direct evidence of malignancy in the right breast lump
No confirmation of fibroadenoma diagnosis in the right breast lump
decisive_items: A core-needle biopsy of the left breast confirmed infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that was estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive

Fine-needle aspiration cytology of the left breast lump revealed poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli; myoepithelial cells and bare nuclei were absent.
response.rationale: The champion candidate, R4, is supported by multiple raw spans indicating the presence of infiltrative ductal carcinoma in the left breast, including cytology and biopsy results. The runner-up candidate, R1, is suspected to be a fibroadenoma based on physical examination results, but lacks direct evidence of malignancy in the right breast lump.

rejected.why: Type 2 diabetes is a pre-existing condition, but not the primary diagnosis.
Axillary lymph node metastasis is a secondary diagnosis, related to the primary diagnosis of infiltrative ductal carcinoma.
Hypertension is a pre-existing condition, but not the primary diagnosis.
